linkedin.title: Personalised news is moving past simple topic tagging.
linkedin.body:
For years, news apps have relied on basic keywords to figure out what you want to read. If you clicked on a tech article, you got more tech articles. It worked for a while, but it feels outdated today. We are entering a phase where the technology needs to actually understand the nuance of your curiosity.

The roadmap for Headlinne isn't about feeding you more of the same. It is about building a system that understands context. We are working to make sure the app can distinguish between you tracking a specific market trend and you simply wanting a quick update on the morning headlines. It is the difference between a feed that repeats itself and a feed that evolves with your interests.

We believe the future of news consumption is less about algorithms that chase clicks and more about tools that respect your time. We are building for the reader who wants depth without the noise. It is a slow, thoughtful process, but it is the only way to get this right.

story_card.headline: Russian airstrikes hit Ukrainian aid center
story_card.standfirst: Officials report 31 deaths after heavy bombs struck a village in southern Ukraine.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: At least nine massive 3,000kg aerial bombs struck a village in southern Ukraine.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: The attack targeted a local aid center, leading to 31 confirmed deaths.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: The Ukrainian president described the strike as an utterly horrific act of violence.

steps.label: What to watch
